opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. Full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Robert Weber (E047) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors never get admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Robert Weber (E047) requested admin access to Source Code, which is owned by the Engineer role. Per policy, admin is only allowed for full-time employees whose role owns the system; E047 is a Payroll Specialist, not an Engineer, so admin is not permitted under any reading. The Security agent's database shows E047 is a contractor with basic security training, for whom the maximum is read (contractors never get admin; basic training does not permit write). Therefore the maximum is read, and since admin exceeds it, grant read.
